role_policy: Original mascot assets and the accepted v4 design direction govern character geometry. Spring/Summer/Practical Learning/Thank You graphics govern gouache surface treatment only. Paint Sol and the whole scene together. The lantern video supplies painted movement reference subject to the current exact on-twos and facial-anchoring rules; do not inherit its eye closures or distortions, example props, counts or layouts.
identity_constraints: Preserve the original 2D silhouette, tip, lobes/notches, substantial red outer shape and nested orange/cream contours and relative widths. Preserve face/body proportions while applying visible gouache brushwork and layered color to those shapes. During animation, small coordinated action-driven body/tip/lobe flex is allowed under the current motion style, returning to reference proportions at settled endpoints.

Keep the normal open-eye design as the original navy #1C2447 ovals, with reference shape, size, low placement and close spacing. A brief natural blink may close and reopen both eyes, returning promptly to those original ovals. Keep the face attached to the body. No whites, highlights, extra pupils, unrelated expressive eye morphs, winks or facial-feature drift.
Preserve the short rounded red-orange arms shown in the mascot examples, including shape, thickness, length and attachment points. Do not turn them into long arms or large separate hands.
Feet are two tiny rounded red vertical nubs peeking directly below the flame body, at original proportions. No lower-leg shaft, ankle, boot-like toe, shoes or fingers.
Keep the same mouthless mascot across every visible scene and throughout motion. Pose and perspective change while character features and anatomy stay consistent.
Apply the painted treatment to those same source shapes; do not copy redesigned anatomy from a previously generated frame.
Keep hands empty in the escalator scenes. Example props and accessories are not part of the neutral mascot.

His face remains part of his body: never slide or rotate facial markings independently, introduce a neck, or reshape the body to simulate a separate head turn. Small bouncy flame-like body/tip follow-through is allowed when Sol moves; layers and face travel together coherently, with unchanged open navy eye ovals and constant stubby limb lengths. Scripted paired eye-gaze shifts inside the face are allowed for that attention cue; they are distinct from unmotivated facial drift.
latest_user_clarification: Move Sol through each short gesture with a gentle connected body-and-tip wiggle, then settle into the supplied ending pose. Keep both feet supported. His filled red/orange/cream layers, face and original lobes move together as one compact painted form. No particles, sparks, brush-flecks, droplets, detached flame shapes, airborne hops or body splitting. During Narrator speech, establish body-led attention UP toward the fixed point just above camera before the first word and maintain it with quiet connected listening idle. Keep the normal-height close-spaced navy oval eyes unchanged; a brief natural blink is allowed. No extra gestures, windup, repeated nodding or camera movement. generation_reference_policy: For a wrong character, use original mascot first and a character-free background. For the current paint-only revision, retain v4 geometry and use graphic references for gouache brushwork. Compare geometry and painted finish separately; a style pass must not rebuild the accepted character.
paint_prompt_wording: Use soft gouache-like brushwork, layered color, subtle paper texture and expressive painted shapes. Define forms through light and color, with no outlines, black strokes or inked edges. Paint every visible subject, prop and part of the environment with the same brushwork and surface texture. Keep clear spacing, gentle light and accurate, readable forms.
paint_reference_scope: Use these graphics for gouache brushwork, layered color, paper texture and light only. Original mascot assets govern geometry; do not inherit sample expressions, props, subject counts, seasons or wide format.
